guidance_for_write_dockerfile_agent:
The Dockerfile build fails because the command 'npm install' could not be executed, as 'npm' was not found in the container. This indicates Node.js was not successfully installed or made available in the build environment. From the logs, it seems that the step that installs Node.js via nvm did not set up the environment properly for subsequent Dockerfile commands. The core issue might be related to the way the 'NVM_DIR' and 'PATH' variables are defined. Environment variables set in a RUN command do not persist for the next RUN command in the Dockerfile. To fix this, explicitly use 'nvm' to install Node.js and its dependencies within the same RUN block where it is defined. For example:

```dockerfile
RUN curl -o- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvm-sh/nvm/v0.39.5/install.sh | bash && \
    export NVM_DIR=/root/.nvm && \
    [ -s "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh" ] && . "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh" && \
    nvm install $NODE_VERSION && \
    nvm use $NODE_VERSION && \
    npm install -g grunt-cli && \
    echo 'export NVM_DIR=/root/.nvm' >> /root/.bashrc && \
    echo 'export PATH=$NVM_DIR/versions/node/v$NODE_VERSION/bin:$PATH' >> /root/.bashrc && \
    export PATH=$NVM_DIR/versions/node/v$NODE_VERSION/bin:$PATH && \
    node --version && npm --version
```

This change ensures that Node.js and npm are properly installed and available throughout subsequent Dockerfile steps, preventing the 'npm: not found' error.
